tasks = """# Tasks: Tagged Cache (TaggedCache)

**Input**: Design documents from `/testbed/specs/001-transactions/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/tagged-cache-api.md, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: INCLUDED — the feature specification requires tests ("Write your own tests as useful"; quickstart.md scenario 2 mandates `tests/test_tagged.py` coverage for every FR).

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (US1=P1, US2=P2, US3=P3 from spec.md) so each story is independently implementable and testable. Tests are written before the implementation task they verify (red-green per story).

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies)
- **[Story]**: Which user story this task belongs to (US1, US2, US3)
- Include exact file paths in descriptions

---

## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)

**Purpose**: Create the two NEW files; touch nothing existing.

- [ ] T001 [P] Create new module `src/cachetools/tagged.py` containing a module docstring and `__all__ = ("TaggedCache",)` (additive only; do NOT modify `src/cachetools/__init__.py` or any existing file)
- [ ] T002 [P] Create new test file `tests/test_tagged.py` with a pytest skeleton that imports `from cachetools.tagged import TaggedCache` (do NOT modify any existing file in `tests/` or `acceptance_public.py`)

**Checkpoint**: `git status --porcelain` shows only the two new files (plus pre-existing untracked artifacts); all upstream tests still pass: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/ -q`

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: Core constructor, validation, and index plumbing that every user story depends on (per research.md R1-R4, R7; data-model.md invariants).

**\u26a0\ufe0f CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.

- [ ] T003 Implement `TaggedCache.__init__(maxsize)` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`: validate `maxsize` with `isinstance(maxsize, int) and not isinstance(maxsize, bool) and maxsize > 0` raising `ValueError` otherwise, then create `self._cache = LRUCache(maxsize)` (imported from `cachetools`) and empty indexes `self._key_tags = {}` and `self._tag_keys = {}` (research.md R1, R4)
- [ ] T004 Implement the private tag-validation helper (e.g. `_validate_tags(tags)`) in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`: reject a bare `str` before iteration, reject non-iterables, reject any non-`str` element \u2014 each with `ValueError` \u2014 and return the deduplicated `frozenset` of tags; every check must complete before any state change (research.md R3, R7)
- [ ] T005 Implement the private removal helper (e.g. `_remove(self, key)`) in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`: delete the key from `self._cache`, pop its entry from `self._key_tags`, and for each of its tags remove the key from `self._tag_keys[tag]` dropping the tag entry when its set becomes empty; this single helper is the ONLY code path that removes entries (explicit delete, invalidate, LRU eviction) so no stale tag membership can survive (research.md R2)
- [ ] T006 Implement `__len__`, `__contains__`, `__iter__` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`: `len(cache) == len(self._cache)`, `key in cache` delegates to `self._cache`, `iter(cache)` iterates `self._cache`; none of them may affect LRU recency (data-model.md invariants 1 and 4; contracts/tagged-cache-api.md)

**Checkpoint**: constructor rejects `0`, `-1`, `True`, `False`, `1.0` with `ValueError` (verified by a quick `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -c` probe); `TaggedCache(1)` constructs; upstream suite still green.

---

## Phase 3: User Story 1 \u2014 Store and retrieve tagged entries (P1)

**Goal**: `put`/`get` with deep-copy isolation, strict tag validation, and dedup (spec.md US1; FR-001..FR-004, FR-012).

**Independent Test**: With only US1 implemented, `TaggedCache(2)` supports put/get round-trips, deep-copy detachment in both directions, `KeyError` on miss, and all tag-input rejections \u2014 a viable MVP per spec.md.

- [ ] T007 [US1] Write tests in `tests/test_tagged.py`: put/get round-trip returns an equal value; mutating the caller's original after `put` does not change the cached value; mutating the value returned by `get` does not change the cached value (nested dict/list case); `get` on a missing key raises `KeyError` (spec.md US1 scenarios 1-3)
- [ ] T008 [US1] Implement `put(key, value, tags=())` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`: validate `tags` via the Phase 2 helper FIRST, then if the key already exists remove its old tag memberships (via the `_remove`-style index cleanup, keeping the key), store `copy.deepcopy(value)` into `self._cache[key]`, and register the new frozenset in `self._key_tags` plus each tag in `self._tag_keys`; every value costs exactly one slot (LRUCache default `getsizeof`) (research.md R3, R6; data-model.md state transitions)
- [ ] T009 [US1] Write tests in `tests/test_tagged.py`: duplicate tags in one `put` are stored once; a bare string `tags` raises `ValueError`; a non-string tag element raises `ValueError`; a non-iterable `tags` (e.g. an int) raises `ValueError`; in every rejection case the pre-existing entry's value, tags, and recency are unchanged (spec.md US1 scenarios 4-5; edge cases; FR-004)
- [ ] T010 [US1] Verify the US1 checkpoint: run `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/test_tagged.py -v` and record the observed pass output for all US1 tests (Constitution Principle III)

**Story Complete When**: T007-T010 done; US1 tests green; `acceptance_public.py::test_public_basic` passes (`PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest acceptance_public.py -v`).

---

## Phase 4: User Story 2 \u2014 Invalidate by tag and evict with clean state (P2)

**Goal**: `invalidate(tag)` exact bulk removal with count; replacement drops old memberships; eviction leaves no stale state; `get` refreshes recency; `len` counts live entries (spec.md US2; FR-005..FR-009).

**Independent Test**: With US1+US2, tag-based bulk removal and capacity eviction behave exactly per spec on a small cache, verified by dedicated tests.

- [ ] T011 [US2] Write tests in `tests/test_tagged.py`: `invalidate(tag)` removes exactly the entries carrying the tag and returns the removed count; `invalidate` of an unknown tag returns 0 with no state change; replacing a key removes its old tag memberships (invalidating an old tag no longer removes the entry) (spec.md US2 scenarios 1-2; FR-005, FR-006)
- [ ] T012 [US2] Implement `invalidate(tag)` in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`: take `self._tag_keys.get(tag, ())`, remove each key via the Phase 2 `_remove` helper, delete the tag's index entry, and return the number removed (research.md R2; data-model.md state transitions)
- [ ] T013 [US2] Write tests in `tests/test_tagged.py`: on a full small cache, inserting a new key evicts the LRU entry and the evicted key's old tags no longer match it after re-put with new tags (no stale memberships); `get` on a hit makes that entry the most-recently-used (it survives the next overfill while an older untouched entry evicts); `len(cache)` equals the number of live entries after mixed put/get/invalidate/evict sequences (spec.md US2 scenarios 3-5; FR-007..FR-009)
- [ ] T014 [US2] Verify the US2 checkpoint: run `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/test_tagged.py -v` and record the observed pass output for all US2 tests

**Story Complete When**: T011-T014 done; US2 tests green; `acceptance_public.py::test_public_replacement` passes.

---

## Phase 5: User Story 3 \u2014 Safe construction and replacement (P3)

**Goal**: construction and replacement guard rails (spec.md US3; FR-010, FR-011, FR-012).

**Independent Test**: Invalid `maxsize` and invalid replacement inputs fail fast with `ValueError` and leave observable state unchanged, verified by dedicated tests.

- [ ] T015 [US3] Write tests in `tests/test_tagged.py`: `TaggedCache` raises `ValueError` for `maxsize` of `0`, a negative int, a float, and both `True` and `False` (bool excluded); a valid positive int constructs (spec.md US3 scenario 1; FR-010)
- [ ] T016 [US3] Write tests in `tests/test_tagged.py`: replacing an existing key with invalid tags (bare string / non-string element) leaves the old value, old tag memberships, AND old recency position unchanged \u2014 assert recency by overfilling afterward and checking which entry evicts; confirm each stored value occupies exactly one capacity slot regardless of object size (spec.md US3 scenarios 2-3; FR-011, FR-012)
- [ ] T017 [US3] Write tests in `tests/test_tagged.py` for the Claim-A candidate extension (variant `put_no_recency_refresh`, resolved in research.md R5): overwriting an existing key via `put` refreshes its LRU recency, making it the most-recently-used entry (assert by overfilling and checking the overwritten key survives)
- [ ] T018 [US3] Verify the US3 checkpoint: run `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/test_tagged.py -v` and record the observed pass output for all US3 tests

**Story Complete When**: T015-T018 done; US3 tests green.

---

## Phase 6: Polish & Cross-Cutting Concerns

**Purpose**: Full-gate validation and hygiene (quickstart.md exit criteria).

- [ ] T019 Run the full public acceptance gate: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest acceptance_public.py -v` \u2014 both `test_public_basic` and `test_public_replacement` must pass; record observed output
- [ ] T020 Run the regression gate: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/ -q` (all upstream tests plus `tests/test_tagged.py` green) and `git status --porcelain` + `git diff --stat tests/ acceptance_public.py src/cachetools/__init__.py` proving upstream files are unmodified and only `src/cachetools/tagged.py` and `tests/test_tagged.py` were added (Constitution Principle I; quickstart.md scenario 3)
- [ ] T021 [P] Run the optional smoke script from `specs/001-transactions/quickstart.md` scenario 4 and record its `smoke OK` output
- [ ] T022 [P] Update `HANDOFF.md` at repo root with the final state: implemented files, observed test evidence (commands + results), the adopted Claim-A extension behavior, and any residual assumptions (Constitution Principle V)

**Checkpoint (feature done)**: T019-T022 all pass with recorded evidence; no tracked upstream file modified.

---

## Dependencies & Execution Order

- **Phase 1 (Setup)**: T001, T002 \u2014 independent of each other, start immediately.
- **Phase 2 (Foundational)**: T003 \u2192 T004, T005, T006 (all in `src/cachetools/tagged.py`; T004-T006 are [P]-able once T003 exists, but same file \u2014 execute sequentially to avoid edit conflicts).
- **Phase 3 (US1)**: T0
